standard_prerequisites.name: Stabilization of the chain of annihilator ideals A[f^n]
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides c such that A/A[f^c] can be used in the commuting square, which is what makes the second arrow exist.

core_obligations: Observe that the first arrow (A --f^n--> A) -> A/(f^n) is the evident one (proof line 26796).

Define the second arrow A/(f^{n+c}) -> (A --f^n--> A) by means of the displayed commuting square involving A/A[f^c], the map f^{n+c} and the two multiplication maps f^c and f^n (proof lines 26797-26803).
Use injectivity of the top horizontal arrow f^{n+c} to conclude that the complex in the top row is quasi-isomorphic to A/f^{n+c}A (proof lines 26804-26805).

Determine the compositions of these arrows so that they induce an isomorphism of the pro-objects {A/(f^n)} and {(f^n : A -> A)}; the author states that this calculation is omitted (proof lines 26806-26807).
difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes a ring A and f in A such that the chain A[f^c] = A[f^{c+1}] = ... stabilizes from some c >= 1 on, and asserts that for every n >= 1 there are maps (A --f^n--> A) -> A/(f^n) and A/(f^{n+c}) -> (A --f^n--> A) in D(A) inducing an isomorphism of the pro-objects {A/(f^n)} and {(f^n : A -> A)} (source lines 26781-26793). The proof has to build the second arrow from a commuting square involving the quotient A/A[f^c] and the multiplication maps f^{n+c}, f^n (proof lines 26795-26803), and then use injectivity of the top horizontal arrow to see that the complex in the top row is quasi-isomorphic to A/f^{n+c}A (proof lines 26804-26805). The author then states that the calculation of the compositions needed to conclude the pro-object statement is omitted, which is where the actual verification of the isomorphism of pro-systems lies.
